findings.en_sentence: Fossils of Palaeotodus date to the Lower Oligocene epoch, when the genus lived between 33.9 and 27.3 million years ago during the Rupelian stage.
findings.es_sentence: Los fósiles de Palaeotodus datan del Oligoceno inferior, época en la que el género vivió hace entre 33,9 y 27,3 millones de años, durante el piso Rupeliense.
findings.problem: Restricts the whole genus to the Lower Oligocene/Rupelian, but the page itself says P. escampsiensis comes from Upper Eocene fossils (the PBDB/taxobox range omits it).
findings.correct: Fossils of Palaeotodus span the late Eocene to the early Oligocene (Priabonian–Rupelian), roughly 38–28 million years ago.
findings.checked_in: enwiki oldid 1380576841 Species section; F003, F004, F009

findings.en_sentence: Fossils of Palaeotodus date to the Lower Oligocene epoch, when the genus lived between 33.9 and 27.3 million years ago during the Rupelian stage.
findings.es_sentence: Los fósiles de Palaeotodus datan del Oligoceno inferior, época en la que el género vivió hace entre 33,9 y 27,3 millones de años, durante el piso Rupeliense.
findings.problem: 27.3 Ma is not the end of the Rupelian (ICS: 33.9–27.82 Ma; the enwiki taxobox gives 33.9–28.4); also the Lower Oligocene is a subseries, not an epoch.
findings.correct: ...during the Rupelian stage (33.9–27.8 million years ago) of the early Oligocene.

findings.en_sentence: Palaeotodus is an extinct genus of birds belonging to the todie family Todidae, which includes modern todies. These ancient species were larger than their modern relatives but similar in size to the modern tody motmot.
findings.es_sentence: Palaeotodus es un género extinto de aves perteneciente a la familia Todidae, que incluye a los todies modernos. Estas especies antiguas eran más grandes que sus parientes actuales, pero de un tamaño similar al del todie motmot moderno.
findings.problem: 'todies' and 'todie motmot' are English words left untranslated; 'todie motmot' is not a Spanish name (and the tody motmot is a motmot, Hylomanes momotula, not a tody).
findings.correct: ...que incluye a los todis (barrancolíes) actuales... similar al del momoto enano (Hylomanes momotula).

findings.en_sentence: Remains of Palaeotodus emryi show a larger body size and proportionally larger wings compared to modern todies.
findings.es_sentence: Los restos de Palaeotodus emryi muestran un tamaño corporal mayor y alas proporcionadamente más grandes en comparación con los todies modernos.
findings.problem: 'proporcionadamente' means 'in a well-proportioned way', not 'proportionally'; 'todies' left in English.
findings.correct: ...y alas proporcionalmente más grandes que las de los todis actuales.

findings.en_sentence: Palaeotodus is an extinct genus of birds belonging to the todie family Todidae, which includes modern todies. These ancient species were larger than their modern relatives but similar in size to the modern tody motmot.
findings.problem: The English singular is 'tody', not 'todie' ('the tody family Todidae').

findings.en_sentence: The genus Palaeotodus was described by Olson in 1976, with the species Palaeotodus emryi based on Oligocene fossils from Wyoming.
findings.es_sentence: El género Palaeotodus fue descrito por Olson en 1976, con la especie Palaeotodus emryi basada en fósiles del Oligoceno inferior procedentes de Wyoming.
findings.problem: EN says 'Oligocene' (as the source), ES narrows it to 'Oligoceno inferior', which the cited fact does not say.
findings.correct: Use the same epoch in both: 'Oligoceno' / 'Oligocene' (or 'early Oligocene' in both if sourced to Olson 1976).

findings.en_sentence: Fossils of Palaeotodus have been found in France and the US state of Wyoming.
findings.es_sentence: Los fósiles de Palaeotodus han sido hallados en Francia y en el estado estadounidense de Wyoming.
findings.problem: Omits the early Oligocene tody from Frauenweiler, Germany, referred to Palaeotodus by Mayr & Knopf (2007), which the enwiki article itself cites.
findings.correct: Fossils of Palaeotodus have been found in France, Germany and the US state of Wyoming.
findings.checked_in: enwiki intro refs (Mayr & Knopf 2007, The Auk 124:1294); knowledge
